id_source: NOT in the the reference pack instance. Ids verified against a reference 1.20.1 Forge jar taken from another instance on this machine - correct for the mod, but they will not resolve in this pack until the mod is added.
no_video_evidence: transcription did not complete for this mod; human_notes below are jar-derived only

order: [jar] tconstruct:pattern then tconstruct:part_builder - the wood-tier entry, before any smelting exists.
[jar] tconstruct:tinker_station - where parts become tools. This is the tier-1 assembly bench.
[jar] tconstruct:grout -> tconstruct:seared_brick is the gateway to everything metal.
[jar] tconstruct:seared_melter with tconstruct:seared_faucet and tconstruct:seared_basin - the single-ingot 'baby smeltery' that comes before the real one.
[jar] tconstruct:smeltery_controller with tconstruct:seared_drain, tconstruct:seared_table and tconstruct:seared_basin - the actual Smeltery, the mod's centrepiece.
[jar] tconstruct:scorched_brick and tconstruct:scorched_alloyer - the Nether-tier foundry line.
[jar] tconstruct:tinkers_anvil - the tier-2 assembly bench that unlocks the big tools. THIS IS THE BLOCK OLDER VIDEOS CALL THE 'TOOL FORGE'.

[jar] alloys in rough order: tconstruct:amethyst_bronze_ingot and tconstruct:rose_gold_ingot, then tconstruct:slimesteel_ingot and tconstruct:pig_iron_ingot, then tconstruct:cobalt_ingot, then tconstruct:queens_slime_ingot and tconstruct:hepatizon_ingot, then tconstruct:manyullyn_ingot as the top tier.
[jar] the tier-2 tools that justify the Anvil: tconstruct:sledge_hammer, tconstruct:excavator, tconstruct:broad_axe, tconstruct:cleaver, tconstruct:vein_hammer, tconstruct:scythe, tconstruct:longbow.
gates: [jar] CONFIRMED RENAME, and the assignment's warning is correct: tconstruct:tool_forge DOES NOT EXIST as a block in 1.20.1. It survives only as a stale lang string and one legacy advancement - no blockstate, no item model, no recipe, no loot table. The real block is tconstruct:tinkers_anvil. A lang-file check ALONE would have wrongly passed tool_forge; the reliable test is blockstate/model plus recipe or loot table.
[jar] tconstruct:smeltery_controller gates every alloy. tconstruct:tinkers_anvil gates every broad tool.
[jar] tconstruct:cobalt_ingot requires the Nether, and it gates tconstruct:manyullyn_ingot and tconstruct:hepatizon_ingot above it.

[jar] SAME CLASS OF RENAME, found while checking: there is no tconstruct:casting_table or tconstruct:casting_basin - they are tconstruct:seared_table ('Seared Casting Table') and tconstruct:seared_basin. There is no tconstruct:smeltery_io and no tconstruct:seared_tank. Alloys are all *_ingot, never the bare metal name: tconstruct:manyullyn_ingot, not tconstruct:manyullyn.
structures: [jar] tconstruct:earth_slime_island, tconstruct:sky_slime_island, tconstruct:blood_island, tconstruct:end_slime_island, tconstruct:clay_island, tconstruct:ocean_skyslime_island - the slime islands, and they are genuine progression rather than scenery, because they are where slime crystals and the slime tool materials come from.
traps: [jar] Do not emit tconstruct model sub-paths as ids. The shared harvest_guides.jar_ids() lists assets/tconstruct/models/item/**, which yields 'tconstruct:base/slime_sling' and 'tconstruct:tool/pickaxe/broken'. Those are model files, not registry ids, and 96 of the 844 entries it returns are junk of this kind.
NOT VERIFIED BY VIDEO: transcription did not reach this mod, so there is no human-teacher ordering here - the chain above is recipe-derived.
